head: a831578baf115a2903a4d5fedfa926aa04621e3b
reasons: The rewritten review-response.md paragraph about the 'second occurrence'/CLAUDE.md-proposal rule now holds up: independently checked plugin/review/findings.py's update_seen (its docstring 'A finding is repeated when its signature was already recorded (count >= 1) by another change id; two occurrences inside one change are one mistake being reviewed twice, not the pattern the CLAUDE.md line is for' and the code `if count >= 1 and first != change_id`) against the live changes/.review-seen.json entry for signature 7cd11e55e64ea40f (`"count": 2, "first_change": "0001", "last_change": "0001"`) — every occurrence of this finding has stayed inside change 0001 itself, so the cross-change rule correctly never fires, and evidence/claude-md-proposals.md correctly holds only the unrelated line-39 nit. No third inaccuracy found this time.

Independent of that mechanism question: spec.md Requirements explicitly requires docs/notes/<N>.md's `verified_with` to carry all three parts (Claude Code version, plugin version, runner). Verified directly in the live files, not just the review's claim: docs/notes/1.md's frontmatter is still only `verified_with: "Claude Code 2.1.278"` (no plugin version, no runner), and docs/notes/27.md — one of the six files this round touched — is now `"Claude Code 2.1.287; plugin 0.3.0"`, still missing the runner. 26 of 32 files were left completely untouched by this fix round. This requirement is unmet for all 32 files on this exact head, for the third consecutive review round.

This is not a flagged concern closed with a decision: review-response.md's own text calls it 'left open overall' and defers the call to the owner ('can waive the remaining gap ... or ask for a follow-up change') rather than recording a decision in spec.md. An unresolved, repeatedly-recurring spec requirement with no closing decision is exactly the kind of judgment call that belongs in front of a human, not something I can treat as settled on the author's say-so.

A structural observation worth the owner's attention (not a bug, but a gap in the safety net): because every recurrence of this exact finding has stayed inside change 0001's own fix rounds, the project's only standing mechanism for catching a repeated mistake (the cross-change second-occurrence rule that writes a CLAUDE.md line) can never engage for a mistake that recurs only across one change's own rounds — the gate's findings check is the only thing blocking on it, and that block has already had to be overridden once this change (status.yaml shows an owner iteration-cap reset).
classification_reasons: Large blast radius: ~140 files touched across docs/, HANDOFF.md, README.md and the change's own evidence tree, even though plugin/ and template/ are confirmed untouched (verifier.md's `git diff --stat main...HEAD -- plugin/ template/ tests/` is empty).

Not a tight spec: an explicit Requirements item (verified_with's three-part field) is still open after three review rounds, with no closing decision, and the owner has already had to reset an iteration-cap park once (status.yaml: iterations_reset_by/iterations_reset_at).

Documentation-only with no code/behavior change and existing tests unaffected (confirmed: no file under plugin/, template/ or tests/ changes) would otherwise argue for low risk, but the open requirement and the sheer size of the diff keep this out of 'routine'.
attempted: Intent — re-read intent.md's problem and proposed outcome; the diff's shape (docs/notes/, docs/decisions/, docs/progress/, two stubs, four live-doc link updates, a PROGRESS entry) matches the intent faithfully; no drift to a nearby-but-different problem found.

Spec and plan — walked spec.md Requirements/Acceptance and plan.md's file list and order of work against the diff and the current repo state; found one genuine, unresolved Requirements gap (verified_with's three parts) that is not closed by any decision, acknowledged as open by the author; the four nits are correctly left unfixed per REVIEW.md ('nits are listed, not fixed').

Proof — read evidence/verifier.md (phase c/d verifier) and review-findings.json/review-response.md for this exact head; the verifier's own grep of docs/notes/*.md and my own direct reads of docs/notes/1.md and docs/notes/27.md corroborate the gap independently of the review's prose; did not cite or rely on any run-*.json/claude-*.json/stderr runner record.

Blast radius — confirmed via verifier.md and the diff's --stat header that no file under plugin/, template/, tests/, .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml changed; the risk is entirely within docs/, acceptable in kind but large in count.

Policies — security-baseline/data-conventions: no secret or sensitive data moved; ux-conventions: not applicable (no UI); definition-of-done: the unresolved verified_with field is a documentation-metadata completeness gap, not a security or data-handling breach.
The tests — no plugin/tests/template files changed, so no test could mask or reveal the verified_with gap either way; nothing here is a fix-type change weakening a pre-existing test.

Verified, line by line against the live source, the specific claim the delegation prompt asked me to check (plugin/review/findings.py's update_seen, changes/.review-seen.json's 7cd11e55e64ea40f entry, evidence/claude-md-proposals.md's contents) — it holds up this time, unlike the two prior wrong drafts.
